hook: Forty tests. One hundred percent coverage. I flipped one character in the payment logic, greater-than to greater-than-or-equal, and every single one of them still passed.
intro: I'm Hajin. The world doesn't need another AI demo. In 2026 about a quarter of merged commits carry AI traces, coding agents write the tests too, and the one number we use to gate releases doesn't move when the tests get worse.
live: This is live at killscore dot hajin dot xyz right now. Nothing here is pre-rendered. KillScore takes the pull request diff, finds only the functions it touched, and plants deliberate bugs in them. Then it runs your own test suite against every mutant in an isolated subprocess. Twenty-seven mutants. Coverage stays at one hundred. Mutation score lands at sixty-three. Ten bugs your tests would let straight through.
survivor: Here's the one that matters. This is a boundary check in the tier logic. We changed it, and forty tests still passed. No model decided that. A subprocess ran your suite and read the exit code. Now Claude writes a test for it. And before you ever see that test, our runner proves two things: it passes on the original, and it fails on the mutant. Verified kill.
rejected: Let me show you it failing. Here the model's test fails on the original code. It encoded a wrong expectation, which is exactly the failure we're gating against. Rejected, and queued for a human. And this one timed out. A timeout is not a kill. Counting it as one would inflate our own score.
arch: Six components. Exactly one is a model call, and its output never touches the score. The model never marks a mutant killed and never edits the code under test. Seven seconds a run. Zero dollars for the score, about a cent and a half when you ask for a test.
evals: Twenty copies of a billing module, each with one planted bug and an AI-written suite at one hundred percent coverage. The suite alone caught six. A model reading the code caught twelve. KillScore surfaced nineteen. And after adding only the tests our runner verified, the mutation score went from seventy-five to ninety-seven. Coverage never moved.
gate: The gate turns that into a merge check. Set a threshold, name the paths where no survivor is acceptable, and the pull request gets a GitHub check and an evidence PDF with a hash over every verdict. Free on public repos. Ninety-nine dollars a month for the release engineer who has to press merge.
end: KillScore. Live now at killscore dot hajin dot xyz.
